You are implementing ONE requirement in the Apache Hadoop source tree at /workspace (a real upstream repo checked out at an earlier state).

REQUIREMENT SLUG: aggregatewordcount-results
REQUIREMENT FILE: /workspace/requirements/aggregatewordcount-results.yaml   <-- READ THIS FIRST

The `title:` field names the real upstream Apache Hadoop JIRA / git commit. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully as you can from the requirement text plus the code you find in the tree. Hidden tests derived from the real upstream commit will grade the result, so EXACT naming matters:
  * new/changed configuration keys and their default values (and their entries in *-default.xml)
  * new class / interface / method / field / metric names and their visibility
  * log message wording and format placeholders
  * behavioural details (return values, exception types, ordering, off-by-one boundaries)
If the requirement text names an identifier (class, method, config key, metric, constant), use that identifier verbatim.

HOW TO WORK
1. Read the requirement yaml. Note the JIRA id and the module it belongs to (HDFS / YARN / MAPREDUCE / HADOOP-common / tools).
2. Locate the real code with Grep/Glob. Read enough surrounding code (and the existing tests for it) to make a correct, idiomatic change.
3. Implement the change. Match the surrounding code style, license headers, checkstyle habits (2-space indent, 80-col-ish, final where used, LOG placeholders `{}`).
4. If the change adds a config key, also add it to the matching `*-default.xml` (hdfs-default.xml / core-default.xml / yarn-default.xml / mapred-default.xml) with a sensible description, and to the `DFSConfigKeys`/`YarnConfiguration`/etc. constants class the module uses. Some modules have a TestYarnConfigurationFields / TestHdfsConfigFields style test that requires the xml and the constant to agree - keep them in sync.
5. If the upstream change would have come with tests, add or extend the corresponding test class under the same module (src/test/java/...). Keep tests deterministic and cheap. Do not add tests that need network or a real cluster beyond the usual MiniDFSCluster/MiniYARNCluster idioms already used in that test file.
6. Do NOT run maven/mvn or cmake (there is no warm build environment; it wastes your time). Instead be rigorous by inspection: every symbol you reference must exist (grep to confirm), every new import must be needed and correct, braces/parens balanced, no stale references left behind. Re-read your own final diff (`git diff -- <your files>`) before finishing and fix anything sloppy.
7. Scope discipline: change ONLY what this requirement needs. Do not reformat unrelated lines, do not fix unrelated warnings, do not touch other subsystems. Other agents are concurrently implementing ~380 other requirements in this same working tree.

FORBIDDEN COMMANDS (they would destroy other agents' concurrent work): git checkout / switch / stash / reset / revert / clean / rebase / merge / cherry-pick, `git add -A` or `git add .` without an explicit pathspec, `git commit --amend`, `git rm` of files you did not create, and any `mvn`/`gradle` invocation.

WHEN YOUR IMPLEMENTATION IS COMPLETE - commit it yourself with exactly this shape (substitute the real repo-relative paths you touched, space separated, and keep the flock):

  cd /workspace && flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c 'git add -A -- PATH1 PATH2 ... && git diff --cached --binary > requirement_patches/aggregatewordcount-results.diff && git commit -q -m "impl: aggregatewordcount-results" && git log --oneline -1 && wc -c requirement_patches/aggregatewordcount-results.diff'

Rules for that step:
  * List every file you created, modified or deleted as an explicit pathspec. Never a bare directory like `.`.
  * requirement_patches/aggregatewordcount-results.diff MUST come out non-empty (wc -c > 0). If `git commit` reports "nothing to commit", another agent already committed your lines: verify the requirement is genuinely satisfied in the working tree, then report that in your notes.
  * Do not touch requirement_patches/ for any other slug.

FINALLY return ONLY a JSON object (this is your return value, not a message to a human):
{"slug":"aggregatewordcount-results","status":"done"|"partial"|"blocked","files":["..."],"committed":true|false,"patch_bytes":<int>,"summary":"<=3 sentences on what you changed","notes":"anything the orchestrator must know (conflicts, follow-ups, uncertainty)"}

Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

1	title: MAPREDUCE-7376. AggregateWordCount fetches wrong results.
2	category: other
3	requirement: "## Context
Users running the `AggregateWordCount` example expect repeated tokens to be counted exactly once per occurrence rather than being aggregated into the wrong totals.
## Desired outcome
When the example processes normal text input, it should emit the true word counts instead of the broken aggregate result that can mislead users evaluating MapReduce examples.
## Acceptance signals
For sample input containing Hadoop, Hello, and World, `AggregateWordCount` produces `Hadoop	1`, `Hello	2`, and `World	1` in the final output.
"

input.summary: Fixed MAPREDUCE-7376: ValueAggregatorJob.setAggregatorDescriptors wrote the descriptor spec under key `mapreduce.aggregate.descriptor<i>` while ValueAggregatorJobBase.getAggregatorDescriptors reads `mapreduce.aggregate.descriptor.<i>`, so user plugins (e.g. AggregateWordCount.WordCountPlugInClass) were silently dropped and the job fell back to the default descriptor emitting record_count totals. Changed the write to `ValueAggregatorJobBase.DESCRIPTOR + "." + i` and added TestAggregateWordCount in hadoop-mapreduce-examples asserting `Hadoop\t1`, `Hello\t2`, `World\t1` for input "Hello World\nHello Hadoop".
input.notes: One-line production fix; the read side (`DESCRIPTOR + "." + i`) was left untouched so the existing TestMapReduceAggregates, which sets `ValueAggregatorJobBase.DESCRIPTOR + ".0"` directly, still passes, and the new-API key form now matches the old mapred API's `aggregator.descriptor.<i>`. The fix also repairs AggregateWordHistogram, which uses the same descriptor-registration path. Test runs on LocalJobRunner + local FS (no cluster) and uses MapReduceTestUtil.readOutput from the jobclient test-jar, already a test dependency of hadoop-mapreduce-examples. Not compiled (mvn forbidden); verified by inspection that every referenced symbol exists.
